# $\mathbb Z_p$ inside a compact torsion-free group

Let $K\ne1$ be a compact Hausdorff topological group with no element of finite order other than $1$. Then for some prime $p$ there is a continuous injective homomorphism from the additive group $\mathbb Z_p$ to $K$.

*Proof sketch.* Take $g\ne1$ in $K$. The closure $A$ of the subgroup generated by $g$ is a compact Hausdorff commutative subgroup, nontrivial and with no nontrivial element of finite order. The abelian case applied to $A$ gives the homomorphism.

Remark (not formalized). The construction gives more: with $x$ the image of $1$, the homomorphism extends $m\mapsto x^m$, and its image is the closure of the subgroup generated by $x$.
